messages:
claudia: Heads up — product asked for private/VPC metrics export for on-prem customers. We need a quick sync on agent egress, firewall rules, and KMS/audit hooks. Who's got bandwidth?

rory: I can take this. Quick question — are we pushing metrics out or can the collector pull?

claudia: Push only for first pass; customers expect agent to push TLS metrics to our collector (443). We can add pull later.

marta: Noted. Also need to support both sidecar (daemonset) and standalone agent. That affects source IP expectations for firewall rules.

samir: Security checklist: mTLS for agent->collector, cert rotation, and envelope encryption with customer KMS/HSM for any persisted batches. No plaintext metrics leaving the host.

jess: From product: dashboard needs node and model labels (node.hostname, deployment_id, model_variant), and we want latency percentiles and token throughput. Keep metric names stable.

rory: For network, customers will typically only allow outbound 443 to an allowlist. We should avoid requiring customers to open large IP ranges. Can we do SNI-based allowlisting + pinned CA?

samir: SNI is ok but some corporate firewalls do SNI stripping. Recommend both: TLS to collector endpoint fqdn + mTLS client cert validation. Also support proxy config (HTTP CONNECT) for customers with forced egress proxies.

marta: Agreed. Agent config options I propose: collector_url, proxy (host:port), tls_client_cert, tls_client_key, ca_bundle, kms_key_ref. Example config: 

```yaml
collector_url: https://metrics.redwood-internal.example.com:443/ingest
proxy: https://proxy.corp:3128 # optional
tls_client_cert: /etc/agent/certs/client.pem
tls_client_key: /etc/agent/certs/client.key
ca_bundle: /etc/agent/certs/ca.pem
kms_key_ref: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd..."
```

rory: That looks good. For firewall documentation we should give two minimal patterns: 1) allowlist FQDN(s) on outbound 443 (preferred) 2) if only IPs allowed, provide published stable IP ranges and recommend CIDR updates via webhook.

claudia: IP ranges will change depending on cloud region. Can we give customers a small set per-region and a JSON endpoint they can curl to fetch updates?

samir: Yes, but must sign that JSON with our KMS key and publish an ETag. Customers can verify signature to avoid MITM. Also include timestamp and TTL.

jess: Also product asks for audit hooks: when agent sends metrics vs batches persisted locally -> we need an audit log event for any on-disk batch write, encrypt/decrypt operations, and outbound attempts (success/fail). Customers want these forwarded to their SIEM via syslog/tls or delivered to a preconfigured HTTP endpoint.

marta: We should add an audit adapter interface so we can plug in syslog-tls, file, or HTTP sinks. Log format should be JSON lines with these fields: timestamp, event_type, agent_id, deployment_id, details.

rory: Practical firewall/egress checklist for docs: 
- Allow outbound 443 to collector FQDN(s) or IP set per region
- If using proxy, ensure CONNECT to collector host allowed
- If using syslog sink, allow outbound to customer's SIEM IPs/ports (e.g., 6514)
- If customers want to reach KMS/service endpoints (for envelope unwrap), allow 443 to KMS endpoints or support offline wrapping via HSM on-prem

claudia: On KMS: for on-prem installs customers may prefer to keep KMS local (HSM). We must support both: call external cloud KMS or use a local KMS plugin that exposes a simple HTTP/Unix-socket API for envelope unwrap.

samir: The local KMS plugin must require mTLS or unix sockets with strict perms. Also audits for key unwrap operations are mandatory.

jess: Dashboard-wise, product wants to show per-customer ingestion status and last-forward timestamp. We need agent to emit a heartbeat metric and a last_send_success gauge.

marta: We'll add: redwood.agent.heartbeat{agent_id,deployment_id} and redwood.agent.last_send_status{agent_id,status}. Also emit redwood.agent.batch_encrypted_count.

rory: For rollout: propose canary with 5 customers in staging first, then 10% of installs for 48h, monitor failures and latency. We need a config flag agent.export.experimental=true to toggle.

claudia: Action items: 
- rory: draft firewall/egress doc + IP JSON endpoint plan (due EOD Thursday)
- marta: PR with agent config schema and metrics names (due Tue)
- samir: security integration spec for mTLS/KMS/audit hooks + signed IP manifest (due Wed)
- jess: update dashboard requirements with exact labels and cardinality limits (due Wed)

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal.tools/infra/checklists/metrics-agent-egress-1775612345 (created by infra-bot)

claudia: Thanks all — we'll meet Thu 10am to review drafts. If anyone finds blockers (e.g., proxy auth flows, corporate firewall weirdness), drop here. :+1:
